# Development Rules

## Conversational Style

- Keep answers short and concise
- No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code
- No fluff or cheerful filler text (e.g., "Thanks @user" not "Thanks so much @user!")
- Technical prose only, be direct
- Use concise, clear, simple language. Define unavoidable jargon before using it.
- Explain non-trivial designs and problems as: problem, concrete example or short trace, then solution. State why the solution is necessary and distinguish it from optional complexity.
- Prefer concrete behavior and small illustrations over abstract summaries, dense terminology, or unexplained lists of changes.
- When the user asks a question, answer it first before making edits or running implementation commands.
- When responding to user feedback or an analysis, explicitly say whether you agree or disagree before saying what you changed.

## Code Quality

- Read files in full before wide-ranging changes, before editing files you have not fully inspected, and when asked to investigate or audit. Do not rely on search snippets for broad changes.
- No `any` unless absolutely necessary.
- Inline single-line helpers that have only one call site.
- Check node_modules for external API types; don't guess.
- **No inline imports** (`await import()`, `import("pkg").Type`, dynamic type imports). Top-level imports only.
- In `packages/coding-agent`, resolve package assets through helpers in `src/config.ts`. Do not use `__dirname` directly; the helpers account for source checkouts, npm installations, and standalone binaries.
- Never remove or downgrade code to fix type errors from outdated deps; upgrade the dep instead.
- Use only erasable TypeScript syntax (Node strip-only mode) in code checked by the root config (`packages/*/src`, `packages/*/test`, `packages/coding-agent/examples`): no parameter properties, `enum`, `namespace`/`module`, `import =`, `export =`, or other constructs needing JS emit. Use explicit fields with constructor assignments.
- Always ask before removing functionality or code that appears intentional.
- Do not preserve backward compatibility unless the user asks for it.
- Never hardcode key checks (e.g. `matchesKey(keyData, "ctrl+x")`). Add defaults to `DEFAULT_EDITOR_KEYBINDINGS` or `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS` so they stay configurable.
- Never modify `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` directly; update `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` instead, then regenerate. Including the resulting `models.generated.ts` diff is always OK, even if regeneration includes unrelated upstream model metadata changes. The generated model data in `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` is gitignored: never stage it, and don't look for it in git history.

## Commands

- After code changes (not docs): `npm run check` (full output, no tail). Fix all errors, warnings, and infos before committing. Does not run tests.
- Never run `npm run build` or `npm test` unless requested by the user.
- Never run the full vitest suite directly: it includes e2e tests that activate when endpoint/auth env vars are present. For all non-e2e tests, run `./test.sh` from the repo root. Otherwise run specific tests from the package root:
  - Vitest: `node "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js" --run test/specific.test.ts`
  - `packages/tui` (`node:test`): `node --test test/specific.test.ts`
- If you create or modify a test file, run it and iterate on test or implementation until it passes.
- For `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/`, use `test/suite/harness.ts` + the faux provider. No real provider APIs, keys, or paid tokens.
- When regressions tests for fixing a github issue, add a comment with the github issue number next to the test.
- For ad-hoc scripts, `write` them to a temp file (e.g. `/tmp`), run, edit if needed, remove when done. Don't embed multi-line scripts in `bash` commands.
- Never commit unless the user asks.

## Dependency and Install Security

- Treat npm dep and lockfile changes as reviewed code. Direct registry deps, including internal workspace deps, stay pinned to exact versions.
- When updating `undici`, you MUST read its changelog/release notes for the target version and evaluate whether any changes may affect functionality before applying the update.
- Hydrate/update locally with `npm install --ignore-scripts`; clean/CI-style with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Don't run lifecycle scripts unless the user asks.
- If dep metadata changes, refresh `package-lock.json` with `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`.
- If `packages/coding-agent/install-lock/` needs regen, run `node scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs` (verify with `--check` or `npm run check`). New deps with lifecycle scripts require review and an explicit allowlist entry in that script; never add one silently.
- Pre-commit blocks lockfile commits unless `PI_ALLOW_LOCKFILE_CHANGE=1`. Don't bypass unless the user wants the lockfile change committed.

## Git

Multiple pi sessions may be running in this cwd at the same time, each modifying different files. Git operations that touch unstaged, staged, or untracked files outside your own changes will stomp on other sessions' work. Follow these rules:

Committing:

- Only commit files YOU changed in THIS session.
- Stage explicit paths (`git add <path1> <path2>`); never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
- Before committing, run `git status` and verify you are only staging your files.
- `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` may always be included alongside your files.
- Message format: `{feat,fix,docs}[(ai,tui,agent,coding-agent)]: <commit message> (optionally multiple lines)`. Message is informative and concise.

Never run (destroys other agents' work or bypasses checks):

- `git reset --hard`, `git checkout .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash`, `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit --no-verify`.

If rebase conflicts occur:

- Resolve conflicts only in files you modified.
- If a conflict is in a file you did not modify, abort and ask the user.
- Never force push.

## Issues and PRs

See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for the contributor gate (auto-close workflows, `lgtm`/`lgtmi`, quality bar).

When reviewing PRs:

- Do not run `gh pr checkout`, `git switch`, or otherwise move the worktree to the PR branch unless the user explicitly asks.
- Use `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, `gh api`, and local `git show`/`git diff` against fetched refs to inspect PR metadata, commits, and patches without changing branches.
- If you need PR file contents, fetch/read them into temporary files or use `git show <ref>:<path>` without switching branches.

When creating issues:

- Add `pkg:*` labels for affected packages (`pkg:agent`, `pkg:ai`, `pkg:coding-agent`, `pkg:tui`); use all that apply.

When posting issue/PR comments:

- Write the comment to a temp file and post with `gh issue/pr comment --body-file` (never multi-line markdown via `--body`).
- Keep comments concise, technical, in the user's tone.
- End every AI-posted comment with the AI-generated disclaimer line specified by the originating prompt (e.g. `This comment is AI-generated by `/wr``).

When closing issues via commit:

- Include `fixes #<number>` or `closes #<number>` in the message so merging auto-closes the issue. For multiple issues, repeat the keyword per issue (`closes #1, closes #2`); a shared keyword (`closes #1, #2`) only closes the first.

Location: `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` (one per package).

Sections under `## [Unreleased]`: `### Breaking Changes` (API changes requiring migration), `### Added`, `### Changed`, `### Fixed`, `### Removed`.

Rules:

tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

The reporting tool generates SVG charts and accepts text that can originate from benchmark metadata, labels and command-line arguments.

6. Preserve the existing visual appearance for ordinary inputs.
7. Add focused automated regression tests, including adversarial input.
8. Validate the generated SVG with a standard XML parser.
9. Run relevant existing tests and report their results.
10. Document the behavior where appropriate.

- No unrelated refactoring.
- Do not weaken existing tests.
- Do not modify benchmark result datasets.
- Preserve the existing command-line interface and supported functionality.
- Prefer standard-library solutions.
- Do not require a complete Pi-Bolt runtime rebuild unless genuinely necessary.

The implementation addresses relevant SVG text-injection paths, generated SVG documents remain valid, regression tests cover malicious and ordinary inputs, existing functionality remains intact, and the result is supported by reproducible evidence.

Do not claim completion without verification.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Turns benchmark results into the charts and tables of the README and docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
3: 
4: Reads the JSONL files the tools append to (--out) from one results folder:
5:   benchmark.jsonl  bench/benchmark.py       startup, headless, interactive
6:   long.jsonl       bench/long_session.py    a long session
7:   tmux.jsonl       bench/tmux_check.py      Pi in a tmux pane, replies streaming at human pace
8:   conpty.jsonl     bench/conpty_check.py    the same on Windows, in a ConPTY (read when there is no tmux.jsonl)
9:   pauses.jsonl     bench/pauses.py --out    frame times and stalls; GC pauses (--gc): rows added where present
10:   plugins.jsonl    bench/plugin_bench.py    a plugin compiled in vs loaded at run time
11:   long_answer-*.txt, large_write-*.txt   bench/long_answer.py, bench/large_write.py (their tables, one file per run)
12: and writes, for each chart, a light and a dark SVG (for GitHub's <picture> theme switch) to --images, and the tables (Markdown) to
13: stdout. Figures are medians over runs. Results taken on Windows (benchmark.jsonl with private bytes) get the Windows memory rows:
14: peak working set, private working set, private bytes (commit) and the rise of the system's commit charge. Where benchmark.jsonl
15: has the process floor (benchmark.py --floor), the Time and CPU tables add its rows and each build's figures over it.
16: --label name=text names a build's column (e.g. --label "bun=Pi 1.0.3 on stock Bun 1.4.2").
17: 
18: Example: bench/report.py results/2026-10-02 --images docs/images --builds pi-bolt,bun,node
19: """

29: # Pi-Bolt is the accent; every other build (an earlier Pi-Bolt release too) is the same neutral, so the eye goes to Pi-Bolt and
30: # each bar's label names the rest. Checked with the dataviz palette validator against GitHub's page surfaces (#ffffff,
31: # #0d1117): >= 3:1 contrast in both themes, accent and neutral >= 15.4 apart in normal vision and >= 12 for color-blind readers.
32: ACCENT = {"light": "#2a78d6", "dark": "#3987e5"}

86: def ratio_text(mine, base, kind):
87:     """Pi-Bolt against the second build: "2.9x faster" for time, "2.8x less" for CPU and memory; None when within 5%."""
88:     if not mine or not base or kind == "none":
89:         return None
90:     better, worse = ("faster", "slower") if kind == "time" else ("less", "more")
91:     if base / mine >= 1.05:
92:         r = base / mine
93:         return f"{r:.0f}× {better}" if r >= 10 else f"{r:.1f}× {better}"
94:     if mine / base >= 1.05:
95:         return f"{mine / base:.2f}× {worse}"
96:     return None

99: def chart(title, subtitle, panels, builds, theme, path):
100:     """panels: [(name, unit, {build: value})]. Horizontal bars, one panel per metric, two panels per row."""
101:     t = THEME[theme]
102:     panels = [p if len(p) == 4 else (*p, "time" if p[1] == "ms" and "CPU" not in title and "CPU" not in p[0] else "amount") for p in panels]
103:     panels = [p for p in panels if any(v is not None for v in p[2].values())]
104:     width, pad = 880, 24
105:     label_size, value_size = 13.5, 13.5
106:     label_w = max(80, int(max(text_width(LABELS.get(b, b), label_size) for b in builds)) + 16)
107:     columns = 2 if label_w <= 170 else 1
108:     col_w = (width - pad * (columns + 1)) // columns
109:     row_h, bar_h = 30, 16
110:     panel_h = 42 + row_h * len(builds) + 18
111:     rows = (len(panels) + columns - 1) // columns
112:     head = 78
113:     height = head + rows * panel_h
114:     out = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" role="img" '
115:            f'aria-label="{title}: {subtitle}">',
116:            f'<style>text{{font-family:{FONT}}}</style>',
117:            f'<text x="{pad}" y="32" font-size="21" font-weight="650" fill="{t["text"]}">{title}</text>',
118:            f'<text x="{pad}" y="56" font-size="13.5" fill="{t["muted"]}">{subtitle}</text>']
119:     for p, (name, unit, values, kind) in enumerate(panels):
120:         x0 = pad + (p % columns) * (col_w + pad)
121:         y0 = head + (p // columns) * panel_h
122:         out.append(f'<text x="{x0}" y="{y0 + 18}" font-size="15" font-weight="600" fill="{t["text"]}">{name}</text>')
123:         top = max(v for v in values.values() if v is not None)
124:         bar_x = x0 + label_w
125:         # Room after the longest bar for its value; Pi-Bolt's ratio sits after its own, shorter bar.
126:         bar_w = col_w - label_w - 84
127:         base = values.get(REFERENCE if REFERENCE in builds else builds[1]) if len(builds) > 1 else None  # what Pi-Bolt is compared with
128:         for i, b in enumerate(builds):
129:             v = values.get(b)
130:             y = y0 + 36 + i * row_h
131:             mid = y + bar_h / 2 + 4.5
132:             out.append(f'<text x="{bar_x - 10}" y="{mid:.1f}" font-size="{label_size}" text-anchor="end" fill="{t["muted"]}">{LABELS.get(b, b)}</text>')
133:             if v is None:
134:                 continue
135:             w = max(4, bar_w * v / top)
136:             # Rounded at the data end, square at the baseline.
137:             out.append(f'<path d="M{bar_x},{y} h{w - 4:.1f} a4,4 0 0 1 4,4 v{bar_h - 8} a4,4 0 0 1 -4,4 h{-(w - 4):.1f} z" fill="{color_of(b, i, theme)}"/>')
138:             weight = "650" if i == 0 else "400"
139:             value = fmt(v, unit)
140:             out.append(f'<text x="{bar_x + w + 8:.1f}" y="{mid:.1f}" font-size="{value_size}" font-weight="{weight}" fill="{t["text"]}">{value}</text>')
141:             note = ratio_text(v, base, kind) if i == 0 else None
142:             if note:
143:                 # (After the value, which is bold: wider than text_width says.)
144:                 px = bar_x + w + 8 + text_width(value, value_size) * 1.12 + 12
145:                 if px + text_width(note, 12.5) <= x0 + col_w:  # (only where it fits in its panel)
146:                     out.append(f'<text x="{px:.1f}" y="{mid:.1f}" font-size="12.5" fill="{t["muted"]}">{note}</text>')
147:         out.append(f'<line x1="{bar_x}" y1="{y0 + 30}" x2="{bar_x}" y2="{y0 + 36 + len(builds) * row_h - 8}" stroke="{t["rule"]}"/>')
148:     out.append("</svg>")
149:     path.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")

152: def hero(tiles, builds, theme, path, title=None, subtitle=None, compare=None):
153:     """The README's headline image: a column per metric, Pi-Bolt's figure large, how it compares in plain words, and a bar for
154:     every build. tiles: [(title, unit, {build: value}, better)] where better is "faster" or "less". With a title, a heading.
155:     compare: [(build, name)], the builds each column compares Pi-Bolt with, one line each (default: the reference build, then
156:     an earlier release if one is among the builds).
157:     No backgrounds and no badges: hairlines between the columns, text in the page's ink, color only on the bars."""
158:     t = THEME[theme]
159:     width, pad, gap = 880, 24, 28
160:     tile_w = (width - 2 * pad - gap * (len(tiles) - 1)) / len(tiles)
161:     top = 66 if title else 0
162:     if compare is None:
163:         reference = REFERENCE if REFERENCE in builds else builds[1]
164:         earlier = next((b for b in builds if is_release(b)), None)
165:         compare = [(reference, LABELS.get(reference, reference).split()[0])]
166:         if earlier:
167:             compare.append((earlier, LABELS.get(earlier, earlier).replace("Pi-Bolt ", "")))
168:     bars_y = 96 + 18 * len(compare)
169:     tile_h = bars_y + 30 * len(builds)
170:     height = top + tile_h + 10
171:     out = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" role="img" '
172:            f'aria-label="{title or "Pi-Bolt compared with Bun and Node"}">',
173:            f'<style>text{{font-family:{FONT}}}</style>']
174:     if title:
175:         out.append(f'<text x="{pad}" y="32" font-size="21" font-weight="650" fill="{t["text"]}">{title}</text>')
176:         out.append(f'<text x="{pad}" y="54" font-size="13.5" fill="{t["muted"]}">{subtitle or ""}</text>')
177: 
178:     def compared(mine, other, better, name):
179:         if not mine or not other:
180:             return None
181:         ratio = other / mine
182:         if abs(ratio - 1) < 0.05:
183:             return f"same as {name}"
184:         word = better if ratio >= 1 else ("slower" if better == "faster" else "more")
185:         r = ratio if ratio >= 1 else 1 / ratio
186:         return f"{r:.0f}× {word} than {name}" if r >= 10 else f"{r:.1f}× {word} than {name}"
187: 
188:     for i, (name, unit, values, better) in enumerate(tiles):
189:         x = pad + i * (tile_w + gap)
190:         y = top + 4
191:         if i:
192:             out.append(f'<line x1="{x - gap / 2:.1f}" y1="{y + 6}" x2="{x - gap / 2:.1f}" y2="{y + tile_h - 6}" stroke="{t["rule"]}"/>')
193:         out.append(f'<text x="{x:.1f}" y="{y + 18}" font-size="13" font-weight="600" fill="{t["muted"]}">{name}</text>')
194:         mine = values.get(builds[0])
195:         shown = fmt(mine, unit)
196:         figure, _, unit_text = shown.rpartition(" ") if " " in shown else (shown, "", "")
197:         if unit_text:
198:             figure += f'<tspan font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="{t["muted"]}" dx="5">{unit_text}</tspan>'
199:         out.append(f'<text x="{x:.1f}" y="{y + 58}" font-size="36" font-weight="700" fill="{t["text"]}">{figure}</text>')
200:         for k, (other, other_name) in enumerate(compare):
201:             line = compared(mine, values.get(other), better, other_name)
202:             if line:
203:                 style = f'font-weight="600" fill="{t["text"]}"' if k == 0 else f'fill="{t["muted"]}"'
204:                 out.append(f'<text x="{x:.1f}" y="{y + 84 + 18 * k}" font-size="13" {style}>{line}</text>')
205:         most = max(v for v in values.values() if v)
206:         for j, b in enumerate(builds):
207:             v = values.get(b)
208:             yy = y + bars_y + j * 30
209:             weight = "650" if j == 0 else "400"
210:             ink = t["text"] if j == 0 else t["muted"]
211:             out.append(f'<text x="{x:.1f}" y="{yy}" font-size="12.5" font-weight="{weight}" fill="{ink}">{LABELS.get(b, b)}</text>')
212:             if not v:
213:                 continue
214:             out.append(f'<text x="{x + tile_w:.1f}" y="{yy}" font-size="12.5" font-weight="{weight}" text-anchor="end" fill="{ink}">{fmt(v, unit)}</text>')
215:             bw = max(6, tile_w * v / most)
216:             out.append(f'<rect x="{x:.1f}" y="{yy + 7}" width="{bw:.1f}" height="6" rx="3" fill="{color_of(b, j, theme)}"/>')
217:     out.append("</svg>")
218:     path.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")

221: def read_tables(results, pattern):
222:     """The rows of the plain tables long_answer.py and large_write.py print, from every run's file."""
223:     rows = []
224:     for f in sorted(results.glob(pattern)):
225:         lines = [line.split() for line in f.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
226:         rows += lines[1:]
227:     return rows

230: def long_hero(results, images, builds):
231:     """Long answers and large files: CPU of streaming an answer, the share of a core it keeps, and the time to write a file."""
232:     answers, writes = read_tables(results, "long_answer-*.txt"), read_tables(results, "large_write-*.txt")
233:     if not answers or not writes:
234:         return
235:     def mean(values):
236:         values = list(values)
237:         return statistics.mean(values) if values else None
238:     def answer_cpu(build, chars):
239:         return mean(float(r[3]) for r in answers if r[0] == build and r[1] == chars)
240:     def answer_share(build, chars):
241:         # CPU over wall-clock time, so the figure is that of the two runs together.
242:         rs = [r for r in answers if r[0] == build and r[1] == chars]
243:         return 100 * sum(float(r[3]) for r in rs) / sum(float(r[2]) for r in rs) if rs else None
244:     def write_wall(build, size):
245:         return mean(float(r[3]) for r in writes if r[0] == build and r[1] == size)
246:     def vals(fn, *args):
247:         return {x: fn(x, *args) for x in builds}
248:     tiles = [
249:         ("CPU, 20,000-char answer", "s", vals(answer_cpu, "20000"), "less"),
250:         ("CPU, 60,000-char answer", "s", vals(answer_cpu, "60000"), "less"),
251:         ("Share of a core, streaming", "%", vals(answer_share, "60000"), "less"),
252:         ("Writing a 200 KB file", "s", vals(write_wall, "200"), "faster"),
253:     ]
254:     if not all(any(tile[2].values()) for tile in tiles):
255:         return  # (runs of other sizes than these)
256:     for theme in ("light", "dark"):
257:         hero(tiles, builds, theme, images / f"bench-long-{theme}.svg", "Long answers and large files",
258:              "Answers streamed at 1,200 characters a second; a file written through a tool call. Lower is better.")
259:

261: def table(header, rows):
262:     lines = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "|".join(["---"] + ["---:"] * (len(header) - 1)) + "|"]
263:     lines += ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in rows]
264:     return "\n".join(lines)

267: def main():
268:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)

272:     ap.add_argument("--label", action="append", default=[], help="name=text: what a build's column is called (repeatable)")

276:         if is_release(b):
277:             LABELS[b] = f"Pi-Bolt {b[8:]}"

279:     # The versions the results were taken with, where the run says (environment.txt): "bun: 1.4.2", "node: v26.10.0".
280:     env = a.results / "environment.txt"
281:     pi_version = PI_VERSION[0]
282:     if env.exists():
283:         for line in env.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines():
284:             key, _, value = line.partition(": ")
285:             # (A line may say more than the version: "bun: Pi 1.0.0 on stock Bun 1.4.2". The runtime's own version is the label.)
286:             versions = re.findall(r"(?:Bun |^v?)(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", value.strip())
287:             if key == "pi-bolt":
288:                 # "0.7.3, Pi 1.1.0 (Pi-Bolt 0.7.3, linux-x64, JIT off)" or "1.0.0 (Pi-Bolt 0.6.1, linux-x64, JIT off), from ..."
289:                 bolt = re.search(r"Pi-Bolt (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", value)
290:                 if bolt:
291:                     LABELS["pi-bolt"] = f"Pi-Bolt {bolt.group(1)}"
292:                 pi = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+\.\d+) \(Pi-Bolt", value)
293:                 if pi:
294:                     PI_VERSION[0] = pi.group(1)
295:                 elif versions:
296:                     PI_VERSION[0] = versions[0]  # ("pi-bolt: 1.0.3": the Pi it is)
297:                 pi_version = PI_VERSION[0]
298:             elif key == "bun" and versions:
299:                 LABELS["bun"] = f"Bun {versions[-1]}"
300:             elif key in ("node", "node22", "node24") and versions:
301:                 LABELS[key] = f"Node {versions[-1].split('.')[0]}"
302:     for spec in a.label:
303:         name, _, text = spec.partition("=")
304:         LABELS[name] = text

306:     long_hero(a.results, a.images, builds)
307:     if not (a.results / "benchmark.jsonl").exists():
308:         return
309: 
310:     bench = defaultdict(list)
311:     for r in load(a.results / "benchmark.jsonl"):
312:         if r.get("ok"):
313:             bench[(r["build"], r["scenario"])].append(r)

316: 
317:     long_rows = defaultdict(list)

320:             long_rows[r["build"]].append(r)
321:     last_prompt = max((r["prompt"] for rs in long_rows.values() for r in rs), default=None)
322:     def lg(build, key):
323:         return med(r.get(key) for r in long_rows[build] if r["prompt"] == last_prompt)
324:     # How large the conversation is at the end of the long session, for the labels ("4.2M-token session").

326:     session = f"{tokens:.1f}M-token session" if tokens else "long session"

337:     def tm_own(build):

339:     def tm_mem(build, stage, key):

366:     cpu = [

369:         ("pi --version", "ms", vals(lambda x: b(x, "startup", "cpu_ms"))),
370:         (f"Per prompt, {session}", "ms", vals(lambda x: lg(x, "cpu_ms_per_prompt"))),

373:         memory = [
374:             ("Peak memory, interactive session", "MB", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "peak_mb"))),
375:             # Own memory at the peak: macOS's footprint, Linux's sampled RssAnon (neither counts the clean file pages a build
376:             # maps, which peak_mb does: Pi-Bolt maps a 114 MB static heap and compiled code, of which a session reads a part).

379:             (f"Own memory, {terminal} session", "MB", vals(tm_own)),

381:             (f"Streaming replies ({terminal}), CPU", "ms", vals(lambda x: tm(x, "prompt_cpu_ms")), "amount"),
382:         ]
383:         own = "Own memory = private dirty pages"
384:     else:
385:         # Working set (resident, shared pages too), private working set (resident and the process's own), private bytes (the
386:         # commit charge: what it has committed, resident or not), and the rise of the system's commit charge while it ran.
387:         memory = [

389:             ("Peak private working set, interactive session", "MB", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "peak_private_ws_mb"))),
390:             ("Peak private bytes (commit), interactive session", "MB", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "peak_private_mb"))),
391:             ("System commit rise, interactive session", "MB", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "system_commit_peak_mb"))),
392:             (f"Private working set, {terminal} session", "MB", vals(lambda x: tm_mem(x, "memory_at_end", "private_ws"))),
393:             (f"Private bytes (commit), {terminal} session", "MB", vals(tm_own)),

396:             (f"Streaming replies ({terminal}), CPU", "ms", vals(lambda x: tm(x, "prompt_cpu_ms")), "amount"),
397:         ]
398:         own = "Private bytes = commit charge"
399:     # Smoothness, where measured: the time between two screen updates while streaming (99th percentile), the longest stall,
400:     # and the garbage collector's pauses.
401:     if tm(builds[0], "frame_ms_p99") is not None:
402:         memory.append((f"Frame time p99, streaming replies ({terminal})", "ms", vals(lambda x: tm(x, "frame_ms_p99")), "amount"))
403:     for step in frame_steps(False):

405:         memory.append((f"Frame time p99, {step_name(step)}", "ms", vals(lambda x, f=rows_of: med(r["frame_ms_p99"] for r in f(x))), "amount"))
406:         if step.startswith("write:"):

408:     gc_steps = frame_steps(True)

411:                        vals(lambda x, s=step: med(r["gc"]["p99_ms"] for r in pauses[(x, s, True)])), "amount"))
412:     if gc_steps:
413:         memory.append(("Longest GC pause", "ms", vals(lambda x: max((r["gc"]["max_ms"] for s in gc_steps for r in pauses[(x, s, True)]
414:                                                                     if r["gc"]["max_ms"] is not None), default=None)), "amount"))
415:     for name, title, subtitle, panels in [

424:         ("Ready to type", "ms", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "tti_ms")), "faster"),
425:         ("CPU per session", "ms", vals(lambda x: b(x, "interactive", "cpu_ms")), "less"),
426:         ("CPU while streaming", "ms", vals(lambda x: tm(x, "prompt_cpu_ms")), "less"),
427:         ("Memory, long session", "MB", vals(lambda x: lg(x, "own_mb")), "less"),

1: # Benchmark and end-to-end test tools
2: 
3: Every tool takes the builds to compare as `--build name=command`. The command can be an executable (`out/pi-bolt/pi`) or a
4: command line (`"node packages/coding-agent/dist/bundle/cli.js"`). Each run gets its own scripted model server and a
5: throwaway Pi home, so runs are isolated from your Pi configuration and from each other.
6: 
7: | Tool | What it does |
8: |---|---|
9: | `benchmark.py` | Startup (`--version`), headless (`-p`) and interactive (TUI on a pseudo-terminal) scenarios. Fresh processes, interleaved round-robin. Reports wall, CPU and peak memory. |
10: | `long_session.py` | One interactive process, many prompts (default 40; 75 makes a conversation of about 4.2M tokens). Reports time and CPU per prompt, memory and request size as the session grows. |
11: | `early_tools.py` | A model that streams read-only tool calls (read, grep, find, ls) with more text after them, at a model's pace, on OpenAI chat completions or Anthropic messages: the time from the end of each message to the request with the tool results, and the whole prompt (`pi -p`). |
12: | `large_write.py` | A file written through a tool call whose arguments stream in 16 characters at a time: wall and CPU of `pi -p`, for files of 50 and 200 KB. |
13: | `long_answer.py` | The CPU it takes to stream Markdown answers of 5,000 to 60,000 characters in the TUI at the pace of a fast model: what a chunk costs must not grow with the length of the answer. |
14: | `long_transcript.py` | Frame cost on a long transcript: Pi continues (`-c`) a session of 0 to 4,000 entries (thinking, Markdown, bash calls and their output, about 2.6 KB an entry; 2,292 is a session that ran for hours) and streams a Markdown answer, fullscreen and regular (`--mode`). Reports CPU, frames and, on macOS, instructions per frame: what a frame costs must not grow with the length of the transcript. `--keys` types while the answer streams and reports the echo latency. |
15: | `tmux_check.py` | Pi in a real tmux pane against a model streaming at human pace: time to interactive, keystroke latency, paste, streaming CPU and frames, resize, Escape to abort, idle CPU, memory. On Windows it runs `conpty_check.py`. |
16: | `conpty_check.py` | `tmux_check.py` for Windows, which has no tmux: the same steps and JSONL fields with Pi in a ConPTY (the pseudo-console behind Windows Terminal), plus the p99 frame time while streaming and peak memory. The bytes and frame times are what the console sends on: ConPTY keeps its own screen and sends the changes at most once a console frame. |
17: | `ui_check.py` | Functional check of the TUI: trust prompt, commands, `/hotkeys`, `/session`, `!` bash, a model turn with tool calls, `/model`, `/quit`. Exit status 1 on any failure. |
18: | `pig_verify.py` | Before builds are timed against each other, checks that they do the same work for the scripted models: what each sends the model (roles, tool names, tool results' digests) and what it prints, for `benchmark.py`'s headless prompt and the scenarios `long_answer.py` and `tmux_load.py` use. 41: 
42: The tools run on Windows 10 2004 or later with Python from python.org (`winproc.py`): every process in a Job object of its own

45: power. Memory is reported several ways, because Windows counts it several ways:

60: 
61: Starting a process costs far more on Windows than on Linux: process creation, the loader and Defender's check of a new process
62: take 10-25 ms and some 2,000 page faults even for a program that only prints a line (under a millisecond on Linux), so the

    already, so nothing is escaped twice."""
    return escape(NOT_XML.sub("", str(value)))

Careful: I used a nested f-string with double quotes inside f-string in Python. `f'aria-label="{svg_attr(f"{title}: {subtitle}")}">'` — the outer f-string uses single quotes, inner uses double quotes. Nested quotes inside braces are allowed in Python 3.12+ (PEP 701). Before 3.12, you can't reuse the same quote type, but here outer is `'` and inner is `"` — that's fine in all versions. Inner f-string inside an outer f-string's expression: allowed since Python 3.6? Nested quotes: yes, f-string inside f-string expression works as long as quote types differ. Good.

But the README says requires Python 3.9+. Inner `f"{title}: {subtitle}"` inside `{}` in an f-string — backslashes aren't used, and quote nesting differs, so it works in 3.6+.

Actually wait, there's a subtlety: pre-3.12 the outer f-string parser scans for the closing quote; it handles `{...}` nesting with different quotes fine. Yes.

To be safe and readable, maybe compute `aria = f"{title}: {subtitle}"` before. Let me restructure to avoid deep nesting — clearer.

[docs/BENCHMARKS.md](../docs/BENCHMARKS.md) for methodology and results.

### Labels in the charts

`report.py` puts text it did not write itself into the SVG: chart titles and subtitles, panel names, build labels from
`--builds` and `--label`, and the names read from `environment.txt`. Each of those is escaped where it enters the document
(`svg_text` for text, `svg_attr` for the `aria-label` attribute), so `&`, `<`, `>` and quotes are drawn as characters and
cannot close a `<text>` element or add one. A label already holding an entity (`&`) is escaped again, once, and shows
as `&`; the alternative, guessing what is markup, would be wrong for the labels people write. Characters XML 1.0
cannot represent (C0 controls, a lone surrogate) are dropped rather than written, so the file always parses. The images are
written as UTF-8, so accented letters, CJK and emoji come through unchanged. Ordinary labels are unaffected: nothing that
needs no escape is touched, and bar widths are measured on the label as written, before escaping.

Its tests parse the generated SVG with `xml.etree.ElementTree`, which fails on any document the escaping gets wrong:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench -p "test_report.py"
```","old_string":"Requires Python 3.9+; `tmux_check.py` also needs tmux. Pin runs to idle cores with `--cpus` for stable figures. See
